papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that unifies several quantum query-algorithm frameworks built on the adversary bound and bounds the power of the weighted-decision-tree framework.

assertions.value: The paper states, as Result 1.1, that the st-connectivity framework subsumes the (adaptive/extended) learning graph frameworks and the bomb-testing/guessing-tree/weighted-decision-tree frameworks.
assertions.anchor: Section 1.1, Result 1.1 (informal version of Theorems 5.13 and 5.17), p.2-3
quotes: The st-connectivity framework subsumes the (adaptive/extended) learning graph frameworks, and the bomb-testing/guessing-tree/weighted-decision-tree frameworks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 5.13 and 5.17, stated informally as Result 1.1, p.3

assertions.value: The paper states, as Result 1.2, that any bounded-error randomized query algorithm can be turned into an instance of the st-connectivity framework with the same complexity up to a constant factor.
assertions.anchor: Section 1.1, Result 1.2 (informal version of Theorem 5.24), p.3
quotes: Any bounded-error randomized query algorithm can be turned into an instance of the st-connectivity framework, with the same complexity up to a constant factor.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 5.24, stated informally as Result 1.2, p.3
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract uses this to place the framework between randomized and quantum algorithms; that placement is the authors' reading.

assertions.value: The authors state that the weighted-decision-tree, guessing-tree and deterministic complexity measures are polynomially related, so these frameworks can never obtain a more-than-quadratic speed-up over deterministic algorithms.
assertions.anchor: Section 1.2, Result 1.4 (informal version of Theorems 5.27 and 5.28) and text after it, p.5
quotes: This implies in particular that these frameworks can never obtain a more-than-quadratic speed-up over deterministic algorithms, placing a barrier on how much these models of computation can gain over their classical counterpart.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 5.27 and 5.28 (Result 1.4), p.5
assertions.reader_inference: The limit applies to these query frameworks only, not to quantum query algorithms in general.

assertions.value: The authors pose as an open question whether st and R are polynomially related for all (partial) boolean functions.
quotes: Open question 1.5. Are st and R polynomially related for all (partial) boolean functions?
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this as unresolved, Open question 1.5, p.5

papers.title_in_file: Empirical Power of Quantum Encoding Methods for Binary Classification
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2408.13109v2 dated 17 Jul 2025; the preprint states a Version of Record exists in Quantum Machine Intelligence.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, discussion and future work; the results tables and statistical tests were not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical comparison of five quantum data encodings in a quantum support vector classifier against LightGBM on several real-world datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report a preliminary demonstration that quantum machine learning with the IQP encoding and LightGBM produce statistically equivalent results for a large majority of the assigned learning tasks.
quotes: we provide a preliminary demonstration that quantum machine learning with the IQP encoding and LightGBM produce statistically equivalent results for a large majority of the assigned learning tasks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a few datasets, run on simulators.
assertions.reader_inference: The introduction says equivalence held for all selected datasets, while the abstract says a large majority of tasks. Equivalence is also not a win over the classical model.

assertions.value: The authors report that applying entangling gates had a negligible impact on the classification power of the model, and attribute this to the QSVC architecture, where the quantum encoding only serves as an analog to a kernel.
quotes: the application of entangling gates had a negligible impact on the classification power of the model.
Although the model employs quantum encodings of data, that component only serves as an analog to a kernel.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the attribution to the architecture is the authors' suggestion.

assertions.value: The authors state that they perform feature selection, through a quantum annealing enhanced approach built on a QUBO formulation, to support the limited computing power of quantum simulators.
quotes: we perform feature selection to support the limited computing power of quantum simulators.
This feature selection is performed through a quantum annealing enhanced approach that builds on a QUBO formulation of the problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Abstract, p.1
assertions.reader_inference: Results come from reduced feature sets on simulators, which limits what they say about real hardware or full-size data.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results figure captions, transfer-learning section and discussion; the physics models section was skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study that trains a deep reinforcement learning agent on streaming weak-measurement data for closed-loop control of a single noisy qubit.

assertions.value: The authors present a deep reinforcement learning approach on streaming data from a continuously measured qubit in the presence of detuning, dephasing, and relaxation.
quotes: we present a deep reinforcement learning on streaming data from a continuously measured qubit at the presence of detuning, dephasing, and relaxation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract, p.1
assertions.reader_inference: This is machine learning used to control a quantum system, not a quantum machine learning model.

assertions.value: The authors report average fidelities of 0.9922, 0.9919, and 0.9636 for the three noise cases shown in Fig. 3, with standard deviations of 0.0012, 0.0012, and 0.0361.
quotes: leading to average fidelities of 0.9922, 0.9919, and 0.9636 for each case, with the standard deviation of 0.0012, 0.0012, and 0.0361.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the trained agent was evaluated in a new noise environment its average fidelity decreased from 0.9636 to 0.8805, and that after further training it retrieved an average fidelity of 0.9513.
assertions.anchor: Fig. 2 caption and Section III-D, p.4-5
quotes: The average fidelity decreases from 0.9636 to 0.8805 with the standard deviation of 0.1874.
The agent fits the new environment, retrieving an average fidelity of 0.9513 with the standard deviation of 0.0353.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that, based on the numerical experiment, they reckon deep reinforcement learning can be employed as a stream learning approach to closed-loop quantum control.
assertions.anchor: Section IV, Discussion and Outlook, p.5
quotes: Based on the numerical experiment in Sec. III, we reckon that DRL can be employed as a stream learning approach to closed-loop quantum control.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own conclusion drawn from a simulation, not a demonstration on a device.
assertions.reader_inference: All results are numerical; the paper reports no run on real quantum hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Classical and quantum reservoir computing: development and applications in machine learning (doctoral thesis, Universidad Politecnica de Madrid)
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2310.07455v1, a doctoral thesis, not a journal paper.
papers.partial_detail: Chapter outline in the introduction and the Conclusions chapter (all 24 numbered conclusions); chapter bodies were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A PhD thesis on classical and quantum reservoir computing, covering agricultural price forecasting, quantum Schrodinger equation solvers, quantum reservoir design and noise, and a hybrid drug-binding model.

assertions.value: The author reports that in a comparison of five reservoir computing variants on zucchini, aubergine and tomato prices from 2013 to 2022, the reservoir computing approach clearly outperforms long short term memory networks and seasonal auto-regressive integrated moving average.
quotes: We have compared five different reservoir computing variants for predicting the prices of zucchini, aubergine and tomato from 2013 to 2022.
Moreover, the reservoir computing approach clearly outperforms traditional forecasting models such as the long short term memory networks and seasonal auto-regressive integrated moving average.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on three price series from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis also says the conclusions extend to other domains with similar series; that extension is untested here.

assertions.value: The author reports that when the fidelity of the final state is larger than 0.96, quantum reservoirs with amplitude damping noise provide better results than noiseless ones, while depolarizing and phase damping channels always worsen performance even for small error probabilities.
quotes: When the fidelity of the final state is larger than 0.96, the quantum reservoirs with amplitude damping noise provide better results than the noiseless ones.
The depolarizing and phase damping channels always worsen the performance of the quantum reservoirs, even for small error probabilities.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study; the same result appears in the companion paper.

assertions.value: The author reports that, across seven families of quantum reservoirs predicting excited energy levels for LiH and H2O molecules, families with higher complexity by the majorization criterion perform better, and the G3 family gives the optimal designs.
quotes: We have analyzed the performance of seven families of quantum reservoirs (G1, G2, G3, MG, D2, D3 and Dn), with different complexity according to the majorization criterion, in predicting excited energy levels for LiH and H2O molecules.
The G3 family provide the optimal designs of quantum reservoirs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result on two molecules from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis calls its results unequivocal evidence of power; the evidence is simulation on small chemistry and forecasting tasks, with no comparison on quantum hardware.

assertions.value: The author states that the neural network framework for obtaining high-energy eigenstates requires training a separate neural network for each eigenstate.
quotes: However, obtaining each eigenstate requires training a separate neural network.
assertions.certainty_reason: The thesis states this as a limitation of its own method, Conclusions item 7, p.230
assertions.reader_inference: The thesis says it proposed a reservoir computing method to overcome this limit.

papers.title_in_file: Taking advantage of noise in quantum reservoir computing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results, conclusions and the start of methods; the appendix proof was not read.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study showing that amplitude damping noise can improve a quantum reservoir computing model on a LiH excited-energy task.

assertions.value: The authors report that amplitude damping noise can be beneficial to quantum reservoir computing, while the depolarizing and phase damping noises should be prioritized for correction.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1 and Section II, Results, p.2
quotes: Our results show that the amplitude damping noise can be beneficial to machine learning, while the depolarizing and phase damping noises should be prioritized for correction.
Indeed, if the number of gates and error probability are small enough, the QRs with amplitude damping noise provides better results than the noiseless QR.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on one task.
assertions.reader_inference: The effect holds only for small error probabilities and limited gate counts, per the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the fidelity is greater than 0.96, the noisy reservoirs outperform the noiseless ones at the QML task, and so the noise should not be corrected.
assertions.anchor: Section II, Results, Table I, p.2
quotes: These results imply that when the fidelity is greater than 0.96, the noisy reservoirs outperform the noiseless ones at the QML task, and accordingly the noise should not be corrected.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on one task.

assertions.value: The authors state that the task is predicting the excited energy of the LiH molecule from its ground state, that three noise models are considered (depolarizing, amplitude damping and phase damping), and that averages are made over 100 simulations.
assertions.anchor: Section II, Results, and Section III, Conclusions, p.2 and p.4
quotes: which consists of predicting the excited energy of the LiH molecule from its ground state.
Three noise models are considered in this study: the depolarizing channel, the amplitude damping channel and the phase damping channel.
Averages are made over 100 simulations.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section II, p.2
assertions.reader_inference: One molecule, three noise channels, simulation only: the result is not shown for other tasks or hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that their theoretical demonstration suggests the benefits of amplitude damping noise will also be present in other tasks involving quantum reservoirs, such as time series forecasting, which will be explored in future works.
quotes: Moreover, our theoretical demonstration suggests that the benefits of amplitude damping noise will be also present in other tasks involving QRs, such as time series forecasting, which will be explored in future works.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' extrapolation, stated as future work rather than tested.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and Section V (discussion and conclusions); the method and simulation sections were not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: An IBM Quantum paper proposing approximate quadratization of high-order Hamiltonians to give shallower QAOA Ansatze that are more robust to noise.

assertions.value: The authors report, from simulations with variable noise strengths, that approximate quadratization yields shallower Ansatze more robust to noise than the standard QAOA one, and that a quadratized Ansatz yields better samples than the standard QAOA Ansatz once a threshold noise strength is reached.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1 and Section V, p.9
quotes: Crucially, these approximations yield shallower Ansatze which are more robust to noise than the standard QAOA one. We show this through simulations with variable noise strengths.
Interestingly, they also show that a quadratized Ansatz yields better samples than the standard QAOA Ansatz once a threshold noise strength is reached.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the price of approximate quadratization is a loss in the quality of the noiseless solution, and that the clique expansion method does not guarantee the quadratized Hamiltonian preserves the ground state of the original problem.
assertions.anchor: Abstract p.1 and Section V, p.9
quotes: The price paid is a loss in the quality of the noiseless solution.
does not guarantee that the quadratized Hamiltonian preserves the ground state of the original problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own method, Abstract p.1 and Section V, p.9

assertions.value: The authors state that circuit depth limits the size of the LABS problem to about 30 decision variables before the noisy hardware samples are effectively random.

quotes: The circuit depth limits the size of the LABS problem to about 30 decision variables before the noisy hardware samples are effectively random
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result for one noise model and a depth-one QAOA, from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Artificial intelligence for representing and characterizing quantum systems

papers.what_it_is: A review of how machine learning, deep learning and language models represent and characterize large quantum systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that the review covers how machine learning, deep learning and language model paradigms contribute to two core tasks: quantum property prediction and the construction of surrogates for quantum states.
quotes: This review discusses how each of these AI paradigms contributes to two core tasks in quantum systems characterization: quantum property prediction and the construction of surrogates for quantum states.
assertions.certainty_reason: The review's statement of its own scope, Abstract, p.1

assertions.value: The review reports that Gyurik et al. construct a family of Hamiltonians whose ground-state properties cannot be predicted by any classical ML method, assuming standard cryptographic assumptions.
quotes: They construct a family of Hamiltonians whose ground-state properties cannot be predicted by any classical ML method, assuming standard cryptographic assumptions.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the review attributes to other work (Gyurik et al.).

assertions.value: The review reports that other work revealed that in regimes in which variational quantum learning models can be trained, one can at the same time find an efficient classical algorithm for the setting at hand and hence dequantize it.

assertions.certainty_reason: A result the review attributes to other work.

papers.title_in_file: Making the quantum world accessible to young learners through Quantum Picturalism: An experimental study
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2504.01013v2 dated 10 Sep 2025. The Workforce folder holds a second Dundar-Coecke paper (2023); this reader used only the 2025 file.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction start, methods sampling paragraph, discussion and conclusions; appendices and detailed result tables were not read.
papers.what_it_is: A study by mostly Quantinuum authors of a diagrammatic quantum teaching method (Quantum Picturalism) with a post-test-only group of high school students.

assertions.value: The authors state that the data come from an experiment conducted in 2023 in which 54 high school students aged 16-18 underwent 16 hours of training over eight weeks, and that recruitment used purposive sampling of 75 volunteer students aged 16, 17, and 18.
quotes: The data was collected from an experiment conducted in 2023, whereby 54 high school students (aged 16-18) underwent 16 hours of training spread over eight weeks.
A purposive sampling approach was used to recruit 75 volunteer high-school students aged 16, 17, and 18.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract p.2 and Methods
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract counts 54 students and the methods count 75 recruited volunteers; the paper's text read here does not reconcile the two numbers.

assertions.value: The authors report that 82% of participants successfully passed an end-of-training exam and 48% achieved a distinction.
quotes: There was a notable success rate in terms of teaching outcomes, with 82% of participants successfully passing an end-of-training exam and 48% achieving a distinction, indicating a high level of performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study of volunteers with no comparison group.
assertions.reader_inference: Authors are at the company that promotes the method; no comparison group is reported, so the pass rate says nothing about how QPic compares with other teaching.

assertions.value: The authors state that they did not measure whether QPic could aid long-term acquisition of the relevant knowledge or continued problem solving after a long break, and that the data showed an immediate training effect.
quotes: While we did not measure whether QPic could aid long-term acquisition of the relevant knowledge or whether participants could continue solving similar problems after a long break from the course, the data showed an immediate training effect.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own study, Discussion, p.32

assertions.value: The authors state that further investigation with comparative groups is underway to explore factors such as socioeconomic status and gender and to refine the teaching approach.
quotes: Further investigation with comparative groups is underway to explore these factors in more depth and to refine the teaching approach to greater effectiveness across diverse learner groups.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states that comparative groups are still to come, Discussion, p.34
assertions.reader_inference: This implies the reported study had no comparative group.
